difficultyRationale: Requires distinguishing YAGNI from superficially similar principles like DRY and Open/Closed when evaluating a speculative abstraction.
explanation: YAGNI applies to capability built for an anticipated but unconfirmed future need. With only one real implementation and no confirmed second provider, the interface's shape -- including methods like supportsRecurring and supportsPartialCapture -- is a guess. YAGNI does not forbid later refactoring, so introducing the abstraction once a real second provider actually appears costs little, while guessing its shape now risks building the wrong abstraction that still has to be reworked.

options.text: YAGNI -- since no second provider is planned or confirmed, the speculative interface and its unused methods should be deferred until a real second implementation forces the right shape of the abstraction.
options.explanation: YAGNI specifically targets capability built for an anticipated-but-unconfirmed future need; it does not forbid refactoring later, so waiting for a real second provider to appear before introducing the interface costs little, while guessing its shape now risks building an abstraction that has to be reworked anyway.

options.text: KISS -- the interface should be kept, but simplified by removing the tokenize method only.
options.explanation: KISS is about avoiding unnecessary complexity in how an already-needed problem is solved; it doesn't speak to whether an abstraction for an unconfirmed future requirement should exist at all, which is the actual issue here.

options.text: DRY -- the interface is justified because it prevents InternalLedgerGateway's logic from being duplicated later, even though there is only one implementation today and no duplicated code actually exists yet to eliminate.
options.explanation: There is no duplication today to remove; DRY addresses repeated existing knowledge, not an interface speculatively shaped for a second provider that doesn't exist yet.

options.text: The Open/Closed Principle -- the interface correctly anticipates extension, so it should be kept exactly as designed.
options.explanation: Open/Closed is about not having to modify existing code to extend behavior, but it doesn't justify guessing an abstraction's exact method set before a second real implementation exists to validate that shape.
